episodes.208571: A series of storms impacted the Bay Area and Central Coast from January 1st to the 5th, causing numerous flooding impacts and scattered thunderstorms. A low pressure system on the 1st was followed by a strong cold front and associated atmospheric river late on the 2nd into the morning of the 3rd.  A second cold front followed on the 4th. A tornado warning was issued on January 5 for the Pacific coast near the border between San Mateo and Santa Cruz counties due to a radar indicated rotation signature. Around 3,400 customers in San Francisco lost power on the 2nd.
episodes.209758: An active weather pattern brought rounds of rain, mountain snow and gusty southerly winds from January 1st through January 5th. There were numerous flooding reports from moderate to heavy rain, along with some reports of mud and rock slides in the foothills. Ski resorts, Caltrans and the UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 1 to 4 feet of heavy snow in the mountains. There was one fatality of a hiker who had gone missing with these storms. Gusty southerly winds of 35 to 50 mph were also observed at times.
episodes.210865: After a prolonged period of light to moderate rainfall across the two counties, a strong atmospheric river brought heavy rain to the area on January 5th. This resulted in numerous reports of flooding and closed highways, particularly in the two county area.

events.narrative: California Highway Patrol reported flooding across Pettinger Road and State Route 12.
Sacramento Metropolitan Fire rescued a drive who got stuck driving through two feet of water in the roadway at Kiefer Boulevard.
Heavy rain overwhelmed a culvert causing water to flow over the roadway on Highway 128 near Highway 1. Approximately two inches of water was over the roadway in both lanes.
Highway 128 closed due to flooding from the Navarro River and its tributaries. The river reached official flood stage around 10 pm on the 5th for a few hours.
The gage along Colgan Creek near Sebastopol reached Moderate flooding with a peak stage of 76.69 ft.

The Russian River exceeded flood stage at the Hopland Gauge around noon on the 5th causing flooding of Highway 175 and a full closure of the road east of Hopland. The river fell below flood stage during the morning of the 6th.
Highway 20 flooded at the intersection of Bartlett Springs Road.
Scotts Valley Road closed east of Hendricks Road due to flooding.
Eastbound lanes of California Highway 37 flooded at California Highway 121.
One foot of water was reported on the offramp from westbound Interstate 980 to Jackson Street.
Babcock Lane flooded just north of Talmage Road. The flooding resulted in a full closure of the road.
The westbound lane of California Highway 116 was flooded at Browns Lane.
